newsitem.title: USA: Russell sees weak results, stock falls.
newsitem.headline: Russell sees weak results, stock falls.

text.p: Russell Corp., an athletic and casual wear manufacturer, said Thursday it expects disappointing second-quarter results, sparking a sell-off of the company's stock.
Russell fell $3.50, or more than 11 percent, to $26.875 on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was the biggest percentage loser in late morning trading.

The company said it may earn only half of the 41 cents a share that analysts had expected in the second quarter ending July 6. The Alexander City, Ala.-based company earned a record $16.3 million, or 42 cents a share, in the year-ago period.
"More than half the earnings shortfall is the result of unfavourable conditions in our licensed products business," a news release issued by the company said.
Russell said sales volumes will likely fall by between 5 percent and 10 percent for the quarter.
Lower prices will erode gross margins, despite improvements in manufacturing efficiencies and favourable raw material cost comparisons, it said.
Russell makes activewear, athletic uniforms, knit shirts, licensed sports apparel, sports and casual socks, and lightweight, yarn-dyed woven fabrics.
